provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Generator: the background is 0 and the shape is drawn in colour 5. A legend is placed elsewhere as 3 lines: two identical stripe rows of per-column colours, followed by a uniform base-colour row at the bottom. The output is the shape's bounding box. Shape cells take the legend colour at the same column offset, and holes take the base colour. Under D4, the stripe direction lies along columns when the rotation count k is even and along rows when k is odd. The base line ends up on the bottom, left, top or right side for k = 0, 1, 2, 3; a horizontal pre-flip does not move it. Reflections reverse the shape and the legend the same way, so position i along the shape box still matches position i along the legend, and nothing needs to be reversed. The emitted program works in visible coordinates. It crops the palette[5] shape and takes the bounding box of all cells that are neither palette[0] nor palette[5] as the legend. It reads the base colour from the outer line on the known side and the stripe colours from the opposite outer line. It then paints each shape cell with the stripe colour at its offset along the stripe axis, and all other cells with the base colour. Using d4 to pick the base side avoids the ambiguity in the archived solver when every stripe has the same colour, which makes both outer lines uniform.
draft_notes.limitations: Two assumptions are untested. First, I assumed common.random_color never returns 0, so legend and base colours never match the grid background, and the legend bounding box is exactly 3 lines thick with the same length as the shape box. If 0 could occur, the legend could be misdetected. Second, if the legend were somehow shorter than the shape box, the extra positions fall back to the base colour. I found no contradiction between the fixtures and the uniform rule. No tests were run.
